items.answer: Immersion is the objective, quantifiable degree to which a virtual reality system projects stimuli onto the sensory receptors of users in an extensive, matching, surrounding, vivid, interactive, and plot-informing way.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Presence is a subjective psychological state in which an experience generated by human-made technology is perceived as real, because the user fails to acknowledge the technology's role and perceives computer-generated stimuli as coming from the real world.

Cybersickness (CS) is a condition primarily relevant to virtual reality that may be caused by multiple internal and external factors and in which a user may experience symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, headache, or disorientation.

Virtual environment is a non-real, computer-generated graphical representation of a real or imaginary world, populated with artificial objects, that is experienced through computer-generated sensory stimuli.

A head-mounted display (HMD) is a wearable, mobile visual display that integrates electronic, optical, mechanical, and audio components and uses one or two small screens directly in front of the user's eyes to place images for monoscopic or stereoscopic viewing. It can be non-see-through, optical see-through, or video see-through.

questions.question: In VR content, what does the factor called visual motion refer to?
options: The extent of the display seen in a virtual environment
The movement experienced by a user in a virtual environment
The method of travelling used in a virtual environment
The sensation of self-motion sensed in a virtual environment
questions.explanation: Visual motion is the movement a user experiences in a virtual environment. Vection is the sensation of self-motion, field of view is the extent of the display, and locomotion is the method of travelling.

questions.question: What is vection in the context of cybersickness?
options: The speed of a virtual vehicle, strongest when sensed in peripheral stimuli
The extent of the visible scene, strongest when sensed in peripheral stimuli
The sensation of self-motion, strongest when sensed in peripheral stimuli
The movement of virtual objects, strongest when sensed in peripheral stimuli
questions.explanation: Vection is the sensation of self-motion, and it is highest when motion is sensed in peripheral stimuli. The other options describe visual motion, field of view, and speed rather than the self-motion sensation.

questions.question: Which exposure pattern to visual motion can induce cybersickness?
options: Brief exposure to calm visual motion
Longer exposure to static content
Longer exposure to turbulent visual motion
Brief exposure to turbulent visual motion
questions.explanation: Brief exposure to turbulent visual motion alone is not enough to induce cybersickness, but longer exposure to turbulent visual motion can. Static content and brief calm motion are not the stated sufficient exposure pattern.

questions.question: Which kind of virtual rotation is associated with more intense cybersickness?
options: Rotation around the z axis
Rotation around the x or y axis
Rotation with lower angular velocity
Rotation with slower visual motion
questions.explanation: Cybersickness is more intense when rotation takes place around the x and y axes than around the z axis, and it increases with angular velocity. Rotation around the z axis and lower angular velocity are therefore not the more intense conditions.

data.text: Virtual environment design can shape the likelihood and severity of cybersickness through six VR-content factors. Visual motion is especially important because it is linked to vection, the self-motion sensation. The remaining motion conditions—height, speed, viewpoint, angular velocity, rotation axis, and exposure duration—help explain when cybersickness appears and how strong it becomes.
points: Virtual environment design significantly affects cybersickness through six content factors: visual motion, locomotion, field of view, content type, duration, complexity.
Higher visual motion, a primary cause of cybersickness, raises risk, and vection, the self-motion sensation, correlates with visual motion.
Cybersickness severity increases with greater height and faster speed; the viewpoint during virtual motion is also important.
Brief turbulent visual motion alone is not enough, but longer exposure to it can induce cybersickness.
Cybersickness increases with angular velocity and is more intense around the x and y axes than the z axis.

questions.question: What makes the way a user moves through a virtual world a content factor in cybersickness?
options: A change in the field of view captured by the display
An increase in the angular velocity of the visual scene
A longer exposure to turbulent visual motion
A sensory mismatch between virtual and physical movements
questions.explanation: Means of locomotion is a content factor because the mismatch between what the body physically feels and what the virtual scene shows can cause discomfort and disorientation. The other options name separate cybersickness contributors rather than the reason locomotion itself matters.

questions.question: How does a user's control over movement in a virtual world influence cybersickness?
options: More control increases presence, and greater presence generally reduces cybersickness
More control changes the field of view, and a wider field of view generally reduces cybersickness
Less control increases presence, and greater presence generally reduces cybersickness
More control reduces cybersickness directly, and presence does not mediate that effect
questions.explanation: Control over motion acts through presence: more control supports greater presence, and greater presence in VR is generally associated with less cybersickness. The tempting direct-effect option misses the presence link.

questions.question: Compared with whole-body motion control, what is the effect of hand-based motion control on cybersickness?
options: It leads to significantly less cybersickness
It leads to an equal likelihood of cybersickness
It leads to significantly more cybersickness
It leads to a faster onset of cybersickness
questions.explanation: Research finds hand-based motion control leads to significantly less cybersickness than whole-body motion control. The other options either reverse the finding or claim no difference, neither of which matches the reported likelihood effect.

questions.question: Compared with naturalistic free movement such as walking, running, or jumping, how does teleportation affect cybersickness?
options: It is found to produce a slower onset of cybersickness
It is found to produce a higher level of cybersickness
It is found to produce an unchanged level of cybersickness
It is found to produce a lower level of cybersickness
questions.explanation: Teleportation, an instantaneous transition, is found to reduce cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement. A lower level of cybersickness is the reported comparative effect, not an increased, unchanged, or merely delayed effect.

data.text: Virtual locomotion can contribute to cybersickness when virtual movement does not match physical movement. Control over motion affects cybersickness through presence: more control generally means greater presence and lower cybersickness, and hand-based control is found to reduce cybersickness more than whole-body control. Teleportation, an instantaneous transition, is found to reduce cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement.
points: The means of locomotion in virtual reality can cause cybersickness through sensory mismatch between virtual and physical movement.
More user control over virtual motion increases presence, which generally reduces cybersickness.
Hand-based motion control in virtual reality is found to cause significantly less cybersickness than whole-body motion control.
Teleportation, an instantaneous scene transition, is found to reduce cybersickness compared with naturalistic free movement in virtual reality.

questions.question: In virtual reality, what does field of view refer to?
options: The speed of visual change produced by virtual locomotion
The amount of scene detail rendered on the headset display
The amount of head movement needed to scan the virtual scene
The extent of the user's vision captured by the headset display
questions.explanation: Field of view is the extent to which a VR headset's display captures the user's field of vision. It is not the head movement, motion speed, or rendered detail.

questions.question: Why can an overly narrow field of view in virtual reality increase cybersickness?
options: It can remove head movement and make users scan the scene less while viewing
It can enlarge the captured visual field and make users see more without looking around
It can reduce immersion and make users move their heads more to find things
It can increase immersion and make users keep their heads still while viewing
questions.explanation: An excessively narrow field of view can lower immersion and cause more head movement while searching the environment, which may worsen cybersickness. The wrong options describe the opposite effects or an unsupported benefit.

questions.question: Compared with neutral and static virtual reality content, which type of content is more likely to induce cybersickness?
options: Content with slow, steady movement and gradual changes in the scene
Content with flat travel and no bumpy rides in the scene
Content with little visible motion and mostly static elements in the scene
Content with fast movements and abrupt changes in the scene
questions.explanation: Action content with fast movements and abrupt alterations is found to induce more cybersickness than neutral and static content. Slower, static, or flat-motion content is not the same kind of higher-risk content.

questions.question: Which virtual travel condition is more likely to increase cybersickness than the same travel over smooth, flat terrain?
options: Travel through clear weather with steady, calm conditions
Travel over regular bumps and irregular terrain
Travel over flat terrain without bumpy rides
Travel through calm content with static, unchanged views
questions.explanation: Cybersickness is more likely when a user travels over regular bumps and irregular terrain than over flat terrain. Flat terrain, calm weather, and static views are not the bump-related travel condition that raises risk.

data.text: Field of view and content type are two VR content factors that influence cybersickness. A wider field of view can increase immersion, but reducing it may reduce cybersickness, while excessive narrowing can make discomfort worse. Content with action, fast movement, abrupt changes, horror, bumpy terrain, or stormy weather tends to increase cybersickness, although some users are less affected by adventurous content.
points: VR field of view is how much of the user's vision the display captures and affects cybersickness.
A larger VR field of view generally increases immersion, but reducing it can reduce cybersickness; excessive narrowing can worsen it.
Action, fast movement, and abrupt changes tend to cause more cybersickness, though adventurous users may have less severe symptoms.
Horror virtual environments are likely to induce more cybersickness than pleasant general content.
Bumpy or irregular terrain and stormy weather are more likely to cause cybersickness than flat terrain or clear weather.

questions.question: Compared with a short VR exposure, a prolonged VR exposure through a head-mounted display usually causes what change in cybersickness?
options: A lower level of cybersickness
The same level of cybersickness
A higher level of cybersickness
A delayed level of cybersickness
questions.explanation: A longer VR exposure through an HMD generally produces a higher level of cybersickness. Lengthening exposure does not remove, steady, or delay that sickness.

questions.question: In navigation tasks, longer VR exposure time does what to the effect of a locomotion controller on cybersickness?
options: It weakens the controller's effect
It steadies the controller's effect
It strengthens the controller's effect
It complicates the controller's effect
questions.explanation: Longer navigation exposure makes a locomotion controller's influence on cybersickness more complicated as exposure time grows. It does not simply strengthen, weaken, or steady that influence.

questions.question: Compared with a simple virtual scene, what is more likely in a visually complex virtual scene?
options: Lower cybersickness symptoms
Greater cybersickness symptoms
Delayed cybersickness symptoms
Unchanged cybersickness symptoms
questions.explanation: More objects with varied shapes, sizes, and movements raise cybersickness risk, so visually complex scenes are associated with greater symptoms. Lower or unchanged symptoms would contradict that positive relationship.

data.text: Exposure duration and visual complexity are two factors that affect cybersickness. Longer VR exposure, including while using different locomotion techniques, increases sickness, and continuous live-action 180-degree video exposure also raises it over time. Visual complexity is another external factor: scenes with more varied object shapes, sizes, and movements are more likely to induce cybersickness symptoms.
points: Prolonged VR exposure through head-mounted displays increases cybersickness and complicates effects of different locomotion techniques during navigation tasks.
Continuous live-action 180-degree video exposure results in higher cybersickness as exposure time grows.
Visually complex scenes with varied shapes, sizes, and movements are positively correlated with cybersickness.

questions.question: Which set of components is needed when a technique measures cybersickness?
options: An input, a virtual scene, and a symptom list
A display, a user report, and a physiological reading
A questionnaire, a HMD setting, and a final diagnosis
An input, a measurement process, and an output
questions.explanation: Cybersickness measurement is framed as taking some input, applying a measurement or evaluation process, and producing an output. Virtual scenes, displays, or HMD settings are not the core components of the measurement framework.

questions.question: What kind of information does a questionnaire-based cybersickness measure collect?
options: The motion features present in the virtual content
The user's heart rate and other biometric signals
The user's observed movements inside a virtual environment
The user's own ratings of discomfort or disorientation
questions.explanation: Questionnaire-based cybersickness input relies on self-report ratings, usually asking users to rate discomfort or disorientation numerically. Biometric signals, observed behavior, and content features are different kinds of input.

questions.question: What is the most common timing for giving a cybersickness questionnaire?
options: After a physiological reading is taken
At a fixed point inside every virtual session
Before or after the experience
Mainly during the experience
questions.explanation: Questionnaires are most commonly administered before or after an experience, although they can sometimes be given during the experience. They are not chiefly timed to physiological readings or fixed points inside a session.

questions.question: Besides being easy to administer, what do cybersickness questionnaire scales help researchers or practitioners do?
options: Understand causes and identify possible interventions
Classify virtual content by its visual complexity
Remove the subjectivity of self-report ratings
Record biometric changes while the user is immersed
questions.explanation: Questionnaire-based cybersickness scales help researchers and practitioners understand causes of cybersickness and identify potential interventions. They do not remove self-report subjectivity, and they are not primarily used to record biometrics or classify content.

questions.question: How do susceptibility questionnaires differ from questionnaires that rate current cybersickness?
options: They rate the severity of symptoms after exposure
They record biometric signals during exposure
They assess a user's tendency to experience cybersickness
They classify the motion features of the content
questions.explanation: Susceptibility questionnaires measure how prone a user is to cybersickness, rather than rating the severity of symptoms currently being experienced. They are distinct from biometric recording and content-based analysis.

data.text: Cybersickness measurement is presented as an input-process-output framework, so the choice of input, the way the measurement is carried out, and the form of the result are considered together. The possible inputs are separated from the evaluation method and the output, allowing manual, automated, machine-learning, or real-time evaluation to produce class or score results. Questionnaire-based input is then described as a common self-report method that is easy to administer and can use established scales such as the SSQ and other related questionnaires.
points: Cybersickness measurement rests on an input, a measurement technique, and an output.
Cybersickness measurement inputs can be questionnaire-based, physiological and biometric, behavioral, or content-based.
Cybersickness measurement techniques can be manual, automated, machine-learning-based, or real-time while the experience is occurring.
Cybersickness measurement output can be binary classes, multiple classes, or a numeric sickness score.
Questionnaire-based cybersickness input uses self-report scales, usually before or after the experience, including the SSQ and related scales.

questions.question: What limitation of questionnaire-based cybersickness measures makes physiological or biometric detection useful?
options: subjective and unreliable self-reported ratings
difficult and awkward post-session self-report ratings
latency-dependent questionnaire ratings
sensor-dependent body ratings
questions.explanation: Questionnaire-based inputs are used less reliably for cybersickness because they are subjective and prone to inaccuracies. Their main concern is not administration difficulty, latency dependence, or a need for body sensors.

questions.question: What kind of cybersickness input is EEG?
options: a content-based input
a physiological or biometric input
a behavioral input
a questionnaire-based self-report input
questions.explanation: EEG is a widely used physiological or biometric input for detecting cybersickness. It is not a self-report scale, a behavior-based measure, or a measure derived from virtual content.

questions.question: Which cybersickness input can be measured directly from the user's body?
options: stereoscopic rendering frame output
galvanic skin response
simulator sickness questionnaire rating
headset tracking latency value
questions.explanation: Galvanic skin response is a physiological or biometric signal that can be measured from the user's body. A questionnaire rating is self-reported, latency is a system-related factor, and rendered frames are part of the VR output.

data.text: Questionnaire-based cybersickness reports can be subjective, inaccurate, or unreliable, so physiological or biometric signals can be used to detect cybersickness. EEG is one widely used signal, and the range of usable signals also includes heart rate, GSR, ECG, EGG, EOG, respiration signals, PPG, and EMG.
points: Physiological or biometric inputs can detect cybersickness because questionnaire-based inputs can be subjective, inaccurate, or unreliable.
Electroencephalogram (EEG), widely used, joins heart rate, GSR, ECG, EGG, EOG, respiration, PPG, and EMG as cybersickness inputs.

questions.question: Which behavioral input can be monitored through axial movements or changes in the user's center of pressure and may indicate cybersickness severity?
options: Head movement
Body movement
Postural sway
Blink rate
questions.explanation: Postural sway is a behavioral input that can be tracked during VR exposure through axial movements or center-of-pressure changes, and greater postural instability can indicate greater cybersickness severity.

questions.question: What does optical flow describe in a virtual reality environment?
options: Velocity change from exceptional motion through the virtual environment
Depth change from object distance changes in the virtual environment
Actual motion from user movement in the physical environment
Apparent motion from relative user-environment movement
questions.explanation: Optical flow is the apparent motion perceived by a VR user due to relative motion between the user and the virtual environment. It is not actual physical movement, a depth cue, or exceptional motion velocity.

questions.question: Which of the four input categories for measuring cybersickness is subjective?
options: Content-based inputs
Behavioral inputs
Physiological and biometric inputs
Questionnaire-based inputs
questions.explanation: Questionnaire-based inputs are the subjective category among the four input types; physiological and biometric inputs are objective, while behavioral and content-based inputs are separate categories.

data.text: Behavioral and content-based inputs are two input types used to measure cybersickness. Behavioral inputs track observable user responses such as blinking, movement, and postural sway, and postural sway can indicate cybersickness severity. Content-based inputs include optical flow, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity, with optical flow reflecting apparent motion from relative user-environment motion. These two types are among four input categories: subjective questionnaire-based, objective physiological/biometric, behavioral, and content-based.
points: Behavioral cybersickness inputs include blink rate, head and body movement, the manner of those movements, and postural sway.
Postural sway during VR exposure can be monitored using axial movements or center-of-pressure changes and can indicate cybersickness severity.
Content-based cybersickness inputs include optical flow, apparent motion from relative user-environment motion, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity.
The four cybersickness input categories are subjective questionnaire-based, objective physiological/biometric, behavioral, and content-based.

questions.question: Which activity is typical of a manual cybersickness evaluation?
options: A model analyzes raw physiological responses
A person reviews questionnaire responses
A program tracks postural sway responses
An algorithm scores content-based responses
questions.explanation: Manual cybersickness evaluation depends on human intervention, typically through questionnaire-based assessment in which a person collects and reviews responses. Automated model analysis is a machine-learning approach, not the manual one.

questions.question: What kinds of input can be used to train a machine-learning cybersickness model?
options: Optical flow, depth cues, and motion-velocity inputs
Severity ratings, onset times, and subjective nausea inputs
Questionnaire, output, and immersive usability inputs
Psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs
questions.explanation: Machine-learning-based cybersickness evaluation can train models on psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs so that the model can determine cybersickness automatically. The other options mix general measurement inputs, content features, or outputs rather than the training inputs stated for this approach.

questions.question: Why is stepwise regression analysis described as a transparent cybersickness model?
options: Its severity output can be shared across sessions
Its input list can be changed by a user
Its questionnaire scores can be collected remotely
Its inner workings can be easily understood
questions.explanation: A transparent model gives clear insight into its decision-making process, so its inner workings can be easily understood. Stepwise regression analysis is treated as an example of such a model when used with physiological signals.

data.text: Input-based cybersickness measurement has two main routes: manual, human-led evaluation and machine learning-based automated evaluation. Manual evaluation uses questionnaires and human review to judge severity, onset, or possibility. Machine learning evaluation can train models on psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs, and transparent models such as stepwise regression make their decision-making easier to understand.
points: Input-based cybersickness measurement has two broad types: manual human evaluation and automated machine learning evaluation.
Manual cybersickness evaluation is human-driven and typically uses questionnaires, with responses reviewed to judge severity, onset, or possibility.
Machine learning cybersickness evaluation can train automatic models using psychological, physiological, or biometric inputs.
Transparent machine learning cybersickness models, such as stepwise regression on physiological signals, make their decision-making understandable.

options: MSAQ
MS-SQ
VIMS-SQ
MHQ
items.reason: MHQ, MS-SQ, and VIMS-SQ are questionnaires used to measure susceptibility to cybersickness, while MSAQ is a questionnaire for assessing overall discomfort.

options: Respiration Signal
Galvanic Skin Response
Heart Rate
Postural Sway
items.reason: Galvanic skin response, heart rate, and respiration signal are physiological inputs for detecting cybersickness, whereas postural sway is a behavioral input.

options: Postural Sway
Exceptional Motion Velocity
Depth Cues
Optical Flow
items.reason: Optical flow, depth cues, and exceptional motion velocity are content-based inputs for measuring cybersickness, whereas postural sway is a behavioral input.

questions.question: Why might reducing a virtual reality headset's field of view help with cybersickness, while making it too narrow can worsen the problem?
questions.reference_answer: A smaller field of view can reduce cybersickness symptoms, but an excessively narrow one can create new problems that may increase cybersickness. Reducing the field of view can be an effective way to alleviate symptoms. If it is too narrow, however, it can decrease immersion and increase head movement as the user looks for things, and that head movement may exacerbate or increase cybersickness.

questions.question: Why does the perception of motion in peripheral stimuli matter for the onset and severity of cybersickness?
questions.reference_answer: Vection is the sensation of self-motion, and it is highest when motion is sensed in peripheral stimuli. Vection is positively correlated with visual motion stimulus, and visual motion is one of the primary causes of cybersickness. This link shows that peripheral visual motion can contribute to the onset and severity of cybersickness.

questions.question: Why might a cybersickness measurement approach combine questionnaire-based input with physiological or biometric input?
questions.reference_answer: Combining these inputs lets a cybersickness measurement capture users' reported experience while also using objective physiological evidence. Questionnaire-based input is common because it asks users to rate discomfort or disorientation on scales. It can be subjective, prone to inaccuracies, and not always reliable, so physiological or biometric input can complement it by detecting cybersickness.
